The Events section of the tree structure enables you to specify the macros called and/or variables set based on key events that occur during NC program file processing. The Events section of the tree structure displays the event configurations of a particular NC control. The Word/Address section of the tree structure enables you to "group" G-Code words previously defined in the Word Format window (Configuration menu > Word Format) with a range of address values, and associate them with action macros to simulate an action in the control, or on the machine. Machine and Control Building Session 109 1 Session 109 Configure Control Rotary Settings As no machine can have the label “standard”, the way machine rotary axes are configured can vary from machine to machine. Most of the time, the machine manual will describe how the machine behaves. In this session you will see how to configure and test the rotary axis behavior. The following settings on the Control Settings window: Rotary tab, control how rotary commands are interpreted (e.g. ABC). Each axis is individually controlled. Options: • EIA (360 Absolute) — Refers to absolute angle positions. Absolute Rotary Direction controls how rotation values determine the direction of rotation. • Linear — Refers to angles on a linear axis "wrapped" around the rotary component. In absolute input dimension mode (e.g. G90), rotary values specify absolute locations along the linear-rotary axis, while the sign (+ / -) controls which end of the linear axis is used. In incremental input dimension mode (e.g. G91), rotary values specify degrees to rotate from the current position, and the sign controls the direction of rotation: plus = CCW, minus = CW. The Welcome Screen has opened file session_109_configure_control_rotary_settings.vcproject Machine and Control Building Session 109 2 1. Machine and Control Building Session 110 1 Session 110 Configure Control to Output Messages By default, when processing G-Code tool paths, Vericut outputs error, warning and informational messages depending on what is happening during the simulation. These messages are written to the Vericut Message Area. In this session, you will see how to customize an NC control file to generate error messages, monitor a certain machine status and use model visibility to have a visual reminder. These methods can be used to add more error checks to your simulation. Define axes to move, open and close the steady rest • In the Project Tree, select Base • In Configure Component: Base > Append Component > Z Linear • Component tab • Select a Color for this Component • Subsystem = SteadyRest Note: Subsystems are used in machines with multiple motion components that are commanded to move via the same G-Code word, for example "X". By default, a machine uses one subsystem for all motion components, assuming they are commanded to move via unique G-Code words. When multiple motion components are driven by the same G-Code word, such as can occur on machines with multiple independently controlled heads, define different subsystems to control which component moves when the motion command is processed. Optimization Session 253 9 Session 253L Learn From NC Program This session shows how to use Force or OptiPath modules to analyze the cutting conditions in order to learn from the active NC program and create Stock Material records based on those cutting conditions. Select a Stock Material • In the Project tree, select Stock (0, 0, 0) • Configure > Component • Stock Material: Select Titanium+6Al4v+HRC37 Optimization Session 253 11 2. Activate Learn Mode to extract cutting information from the NC program • Ribbon Bar > Optimize tab > Optimize group > Optimize Control • Mode: use pull-down and select Learn From NC Program Note: Learn From NC Program turns Optimization modules "On" and automatically creates a new Tool Library file for the "current" project file. The Stock Material records in the Tool Library file that is created can then be manually fine- tuned using features in the Optimization window, and then used to optimize the NC program. • Optimized File: *.opti • Tool Learn Library: select the Browse icon and set path and file name • Limit by: check Chip Thickness and Force • Force Lean Percentile: Aggressive (95) • Select the Graphs button • Select OK Notice that the OPTI light indicates that Optimization Learn Mode is active and the message in the message area Optimization Session 253 12 3. Setup the display of Vericut windows and set Graph Cutting Conditions • Setup the display of the Vericut as desired Note: The Graphs window which enables you to view the Cutting Conditions for the selected cutting condition. VDAF Session 501 9 • Continue to select Play until simulation stops at line #143 Note: At line #143 the hole is drilled twice and the fastener is inserted twice! Attempted to drill too close to an existing hole at line 143 • Continue to select Play until simulation stops at line #223 Note: At line #223 the cycle M500 is expecting the first stack thickness to be 7.7 and the Skin at this point measured at 10.585! The material is getting thicker, same symptom as previous point but here we also tried to insert a fastener! Stack 1 thickness 10.585 does not match program thickness 7.7 at line 223 • Continue to select Play until simulation stops at line #2098 Note: At line #2098 the cycle M500 is inserting the fastener ID = 5 which grip range is 10 – 15. At this point the total stack is 16.99! Stack thickness 16.99 exceeds fastener 5's maximum grip length 15 at line 2098. Note: The features in the Project Tree > Drilling & Fastening branch allow you to specify an existing fastener model file and setting specific to that fastener. VDAF Session 501 10 • Continue to select Play until simulation stops at line #2187 Note: At line #2187 the cycle M500 is trying to insert the fastener ID = 1 with a countersink shape in a cylindrical hole not countersink Fastener 1's countersink type does not match hole's at line 2187. • Continue to select Play until simulation stops at the end. Other errors are encountered but we will how we can review all errors at the end of the simulation… Do not reset the simulation! • During the simulation move the Animation slider bar to speed up or slow down the simulation VDAF Session 501 11 Sort messages in Vericut logger by error type • From right end of the Vericut Logger select the Analyze message tab Note: The Ananlyze message tab provides all messages i…

讲义原文摘录：
Verification Session 10MT 1 Session 10MT Add NC Programs and define Work Offset A Vericut simulation requires that the below Setup data be addressed. Required: Stock, Tools, NC Program and Work Offset Optional: Fixture and Design In this session you will learn how to use the Project Tree to Setup a Vericut simulation by adding a NC Program and by defining (2) Work Offsets. The Welcome Screen has opened file millturn_session_10mt_ncprogram_workoffset.vcproject 1. Load NC Program file • Project tree, select NC Programs • Configure panel > Add NC Program Files… Note: The Add NC Program Files option will display the NC Programs file selection window enabling you to add one, or more, NC programs to the setup. Verification Session 10MT 2 • Shortcut = Training Tip: Use the Search to reduce the list of visible files. • File = millturn_program.tap • Select OK • Select Reset Model to update the NC Program window Verification Session 10MT 3 2. Add Coordinate Systems G54 and G55 to represent the NC Program origins • Project tree, select Coordinate Systems • Configure panel > Add New CSYS • Project tree, with the cursor on the new Csys1, right mouse click, Rename, G54 • Configure panel > Position = 0 0 5.75 • Configure panel > Add New CSYS • Project tree, with the cursor on the new Csys1, right mouse click, Rename, G55 • Configure panel > Attach Coordinate System To = Sub_Stock • Configure panel > Position = 0 0 -0.5 Verification Session 10MT 4 3. Define Work Offsets G54 and G55 • Project tree, select G54 • Right mouse click > Add New Offset Note: The features on the Configure G-Code Offsets table menu enable you to add a new G-Code Offset table record to the offset table highlighted in the Project Tree. G-Code Offsets tables are used to store work offsets or shift offsets specific …

Verification Session 11L 5 • Ribbon Bar > View > Orient group > play with ZX View and XZ View Note: Vericut uses a pre-defined "Relief Angle" of 5 degrees for all inserts created with Tool Manager. Note: Use the Undo and Redo icons to “undo” or “redo” changes made in Tool Manager. The icon will be grayed out until a change is made in Tool Manager. Once a change is made, the icon will display as shown here. There is no limit to the number of “undo” actions that you can “redo” Verification Session 11L 6 Now let’s address the holder • From the Tool List select Holder Note: To run a Vericut simulation a holder model is not required. If you wish to have a holder model for the simulation, the most popular options are to: • Use (Block) values to represent an overall length, width, and height of your holder • Use the (Sweep Profile) option to access Profile Sketcher window and create a holder by sweeping a defined profile a specific distance • Use the (Model File) option to browse existing model file Verification Session 11L 7 For this session we will use (Block) values. But we encourage you to play with the other holder model options. • LWH = 6, .25, 1; Note: as you enter values the Tool Display area updates The Holder and Cutter are now assembled the way we want and now we need to set the Gage Point and add a Description. • From the Tool Table select 1 > Tool Information • Select the Arrow new to the Gage Point field • Select on the holder as shown below Note: The Gage Point is the point on the tool assembly that will connect with the Turret station mount point. If the Gage Point is set to 0, the tool will appear inside the machine Turret as it will connect to the tip of the tool. Verification Session 11L 8 • Select the Description field • Enter 60 DEG, 0.06" RAD. ROUGH INSER…

topic: VERICUT 官方培训 Session 11L-Create a Tool Library p9-12
content:
【VERICUT 9.6 官方培训讲义】Session 11L-Create a Tool Library（第 9-12 页 / 共 18 页）。
课程类别：verification。课程编号 Session 11L。
讲义原文摘录：
Verification Session 11L 9 Note: The Ribbon Bar > Utilities tab > Preferences group > Preferences command button opens the Preferences window, enabling you to control how information in the Tool Manager is displayed. Note: Mark as Default is used to specify an existing tool as the default tool for that tool category. Default tools become the base tool whenever a new tool is added in the Tool Manager. Each tool category can have only one default tool at most. Once Mark as Default is selected, the file ‘default_tools.prefs’ is added to the User preferences at the ‘%APPDATA%/Roaming/CGTech’ location. The file is updated whenever a new default is selected. Marking a tool as a default cannot be undone. That selected tool remains as the default for that tool category until a new default is selected so care must be taken when selecting a default. Imported elements of a tool (such as CAD, SOR, or Sweep) will not be carried over to the default tool preference file. Cutters and inserts are also not carried over meaning that cutters and inserts do not become the default tool components for their category. Holders are carried over unless “Add Holder(s) With New Tool” is toggled on (checked) in the ‘Preferences’ dialog of Tool Manager. Verification Session 11L 10 3. Save the Tool Library • Ribbon Bar > Tool tab > File group > Save As • Shortcut = Working Directory • File = lathe_session_11l_create_tool_library.tls • Save Note: The Save Encrypted option allows the user to save an encrypted copy of his Tool Manager file. The encrypted (.xtls) file can be used in Vericut, but cannot be modified. The Tool List can be expanded to see tool’s hierarchy, but only the main Tool Information panel can be seen for each tool. The Save Encrypted is one-way process, meaning there is no “decryption…

topic: VERICUT 官方培训 Session 11L-Create a Tool Library p17-18
content:

讲义原文摘录：
Verification Session 11L 17 6. Save the Tool Library and transfer to current session • Ribbon Bar > Tool tab > File group > Save File • Close Tool Manager 7. Play the simulation • Reset Model This will update the tools on the machine turret. Play • Expand (+) Tooling branch in Project Tree to see the Tools Used feature Note: The Tools Used feature enables you to see at a glance the tools that are being used for the “current” Setup. At each tool change in the simulation, an image representing the tool component type along with the tool’s ID is added to the Tooling branch in the Project Tree as shown in the picture below. The Tool Manager’s Description field will be displayed in The Project Tree when you hold the cursor over a tool in the list. Verification Session 11L 18 • Select the Tooling branch in Project Tree, in the Configure panel check Translucent • Reset Model • Play Setting the Tool display to translucent make it easier to see what is occurring in the simulation. 8. Save project settings • Ribbon Bar > File tab > Project File group > Save As • Shortcut = Working Directory • File = lathe_session_11l_create_tool_library.vcproject • Save Conclusion In this session you have learned how to use the Project Tree to Setup a Vericut simulation by building cutting tools, you have built different types of turning tool assemblies using Tool Manager.

Define the Stock model • In the Project Tree, select Stock (0, 0, 0) • In the Configure Component : Stock > Add Model > Cylinder • Height (Z) = 2.1 • Radius = 1.2 • Press the Enter key on your keyboard • In the Configure Component : Stock > Translate Tab • Position = 0 0 4.2 17. Load NC Program file • In the Project tree, select NC Programs • In the Configure NC Programs > Add NC Program Files… • Shortcut = Training • File = lathe_program.mcd • OK • Reset Model Verification Session 17L 22 19. When combined with a Machine file, Vericut can simulate how a NC machining center will respond to GCode NC program files. 3. 讲义原文摘录：
Verification Session 22 1 Session 22 Probe Programming The "end product" of Vericut's Probe Programming functionality is to generate probe cycles generate an NC program (.mcd file) using the probe cycles generated. The intention is to run the probing program with the part still on the CNC machine to verify what has just been cut correctly to the design print to ensure that the job is proceeding as intended. If a discrepancy is found, no additional time will be wasted on subsequent machining. This goal can be reached quickly if the probing is performed on the machine and by the machine, using one or more probes. This session shows how to generate a probe NC Program. The Welcome Screen has opened file session_22_probe_programming.vcproject Verification Session 22 2 1. Play simulation • Play 2. topic: VERICUT 官方培训 Session 2MT-Monitor VERICUT Simulation p1-4
content:
【VERICUT 9.6 官方培训讲义】Session 2MT-Monitor VERICUT Simulation（第 1-4 页 / 共 15 页）。
课程类别：verification。课程编号 Session 2MT。
讲义原文摘录：
Verification Session 2MT 1 Session 2MT Monitor Vericut Simulation This session will teach you how to monitor what is happening in the simulation by stopping at certain events and displaying some of Vericut’s monitoring tools. The Welcome Screen has opened file millturn_session_day1.vcproject Verification Session 2MT 2 1. Display the Driven Point Zero Axis • In the Graphic Area select the Machine view • View Cube, select Front face • In the Graphic Area right mouse click and select Display Axes > Driven Point Zero • In the Graphic Area right mouse click and select Display Axes > Clear CSYS Note: This axis displays the "driven point" and the Program Zero location. The X, Y, Z Driven Point Zero axis represents where the Program Zero is located and the icon illustrates what is being driven, typically the tool tip or the turret face. Verification Session 2MT 3 2. View the NC program • Ribbon Bar > Info tab > Info group > NC Program Note: The NC Program window displaying the NC program file being simulated. In this window, you can scroll through the entire file to see all the records, search for text forward and backward, print, and more. An arrow pointer indicates the current NC Program record being processed. The window is updated when a new NC program file is processed, such as when multiple NC program files are to be simulated. • Dock the NC Program window Verification Session 2MT 4 3. Step through NC program until the first tool is loaded • Simulation Controls > Single Step until G361 B0. D2. The Driven Point is still at the spindle face, this is because tool offset has not been applied yet. • Single Step until G43 H1. G43 activates the offset for the tool and Driven Point moves to the tip of the tool.

Re-play the simulation from the beginning • Simulation Controls > Reset Model • Yes • Play The simulation stops at G361 B0. D2. in the NC program window. Also notice that a “Program halted at tool change” message is displayed in the Message Area. • Play The simulation will continue until the next tool change in the NC program. 6. Remove the display of the Driven Point axis • In the Graphic Area, right mouse click and select Display Axes > Driven Point Zero Verification Session 2MT 8 7. Display the Status window • Select the icon from the Quick Access Toolbar Note: This panel provides status information about the simulation and what would be occurring on the CNC machine. The information displayed can be configured. The status window displays some very important information about the machining process. The Feedrate displayed is the last feedrate value encountered in the program. The Local X Y Z B values display the position of the tool relative to the NC Program Zero The Time is useful to know the machining time. The Tool ID is the active tool Note: For more information on the available configuration options and descriptions see Vericut Help - Info Menu - Status window,…

课程类别：verification。课程编号 Session 3L。
讲义原文摘录：
Verification Session 3L 1 Session 3L Find and Detect Errors The main reason we use simulation is to detect all the errors in the NC program before it goes to the machine. Vericut provides many ways to detect errors and precisely find which line in the NC program caused them. We cannot always rely on a visual red mark on the part to indicate an error; the red mark might be removed by the subsequent machining operation. Vericut keeps a history of every event including the errors. In this session you will learn how to detect the errors in the simulation, and how to find the blocks in the program responsible for the errors. The Welcome Screen has opened file lathe_session_day1.vcproject. Verification Session 3L 2 1. Check for syntax errors in NC Program • Select the Feature Search icon, type syn as shown below Note: clicking the Feature Search option expands a search bar that can be used to find any feature in Vericut. Options related to entered search queries are displayed and can be clicked so that Vericut navigates directly to those features. Hovering over the feature gives it location within the ribbon. • Select Perform Syntax Check Note: Many of Vericut’s functions output temporary messages or prompts to assist you with using the feature. These messages and prompts are displayed in the space below the Animations Control features as shown in the picture below. Note: The Perform Syntax Check option causes Vericut to check all NC program and NC Subroutine files referenced by the “current” setup for syntax errors. Each syntax error that is found is written to the Message Area and a summary showing the number of syntax errors found is displayed directly below the Message Area. Verification Session 3L 3 Vericut can also be set to automatically check for syntax error when a p…

Verification Session 3L 5 3. Configure Vericut to stop the simulation at each error • Right mouse click on Play to open the Start/Stop Options • Check Stop At > Max Errors • Check Stop At > Max Warnings • Right mouse click on Play to close the Start/Stop Options Verification Session 3L 6 4. Cut until the first error • Play A message is displayed in the message logger: Error: Cutter of the tool "1" collided with "Jaws" at line: (23) N1100 Z-1.81 Program halted at machine collision • From Workpiece view, Ribbon Bar > View tab > Display group > Spun Part Display, do the same from Machine View • Continue to press Play until the end of file is reached. Tip: When the motion is stopped before the end of the motion, a yellow Pause button; indicates that the motion block is not completed. The Collision (COLL) light turns from green to red to indicate a collision on the current light; it will later turn yellow to indicate that a collision occurred. Verification Session 3L 7 Stopping at every error is very useful to avoid missing an error, but it requires your attention at all times. In our competitive environment, it is difficult to devote our undivided attention to the simulation. We often need to launch the simulation and then come back when it is completed and review the errors. 5. Configure Vericut not to stop the simulation at each error • Un-check all Stop At • Reset Model • Move the Animation slider to the right; this will refresh the animation after multiple lines of the NC program. Verification Session 3L 8 6. Review the NC Program Alerts • Play Notice that in the Project Tree the NC Program has turned red, this indicates that errors were detected during the processing of the NC Program Notice that in the NC Program window, the Go To Error icons are no longer greyed out.…

Note: For more information on the available configuration options and descriptions see Vericut Help – Analysis Menu - AUTO-DIFF • Set Gouge = .01 • Set color = 1:Red Note: With these settings, any gouges deeper than .01” will be reported as an error and shown in red. topic: VERICUT 官方培训 Session 8-Create Coordinate Systems p1-4
content:
【VERICUT 9.6 官方培训讲义】Session 8-Create Coordinate Systems（第 1-4 页 / 共 15 页）。
课程类别：verification。课程编号 Session 8。
讲义原文摘录：
Verification Session 8 1 Session 8 Create Coordinate Systems A Coordinate System (CSYS) in Vericut represents a point in space and an orientation represented by the 3 axes. It can be created in relation to any machine component but is usually defined relative to the Stock component. It can be referenced to represent the origin of a NC Program, as a reference origin for X-Caliper measurements and also can be used to create a transition to move models. You will see the multiple applications of the CSYS in the subsequent training sessions. This session will concentrate on the creation of the CSYS. The Welcome Screen has opened file session_8_create_coordinate_systems.vcproject 1. Play the simulation • Play Verification Session 8 2 2. Add a new Coordinate System • In the Project tree, select Coordinate Systems • Configure Coordinate Systems > Add New CSYS A new CSYS named Csys1 is added: • In the Project tree, select Csys 1 • In the Configure Coordinate Systems: Csys 1 > Position = 0 0 200 • Press the Enter key on your keyboard. Verification Session 8 3 3. Add a CSYS at the left corner of the fixture • In the Configure Coordinate Systems > Add New CSYS • In the Project tree, select Csys 2 • Select arrow next to Position field • Pick the corner of the fixture as shown below Verification Session 8 4 4. Modify Csys1 to be on the corner of the inclined plane • In the Project tree, select Csys 1 • Configure > Construct tab • Origin (XYZ), select 3 Planes from the pull-down menu Notice that the temporary messages area is indicating that you can now select on a feature • Pick 3 planes to define the corner The Temporary display represents the Origin Primary and Secondary Axis

【VERICUT 9.6 官方培训讲义】Session 8-Create Coordinate Systems（第 9-12 页 / 共 15 页）。
课程类别：verification。课程编号 Session 8。
讲义原文摘录：
Verification Session 8 9 • Update • Secondary Axis (IJK), select Plane/Plane from the pull-down menu This will define a vector intersecting 2 planes • Pick planes as shown below • Select Update Verification Session 8 10 6. Use the Transform Menu to move a CSYS • In the Project tree, select Coordinate Systems • Configure Coordinate Systems > Add New CSYS A new CSYS named Csys3 is added: • Select Transform Menu Note: The Transform Menu allows users to change the position and angles of certain objects in a setup, including machine parts, tools, stocks, and csys’s. It is able to be used in machine setups, the Assembly Manager, The Tool Manager, and the Tool Change Lists dialog. For full Verification Session 8 11 • Snap the CSYS Origin to a 3D object Note: You can snap the object to another 3D object’s center faces, center edges, and corners by hovering the mouse over the transform CSYS Origin, then clicking and dragging. As you drag the transform CSYS above 3D objects, you will notice it try to snap to them. You can release the mouse button to apply the snap. • Play with the Snap CSYS Origin feature by selecting different locations in order to become more familiar with this feature Verification Session 8 12 CSYS Translation along a Single Axis • Check Enable Translation Increment and set a value, then over your mouse over 1 of the 3 Transform CSYS arrows. You should see the arrow outline highlight light-blue, indicating you can click on it. Click and hold the left mouse button, and drag your mouse to move the object along the axis. • Play with the CSYS Translation along a Single Axis feature by selecting different locations in order to become more familiar with this feature

topic: VERICUT 官方培训 Session 8-Create Coordinate Systems p13-15
content:
【VERICUT 9.6 官方培训讲义】Session 8-Create Coordinate Systems（第 13-15 页 / 共 15 页）。
课程类别：verification。课程编号 Session 8。
讲义原文摘录：
Verification Session 8 13 CSYS Translation along Two Axes • To translate along two axes, hover the mouse over one of the small planes that surround the transform CSYS origin. Once one of them is highlighted, you can click and drag to move the object along the plane. This time, you will see two guidelines, and two numbers show up to the top-right of the csys. One for one axis, and another for the other axis, color coded to the axes. Translation incrementing also applies here, and you will see cross sections appear along both axis guidelines. • Play with the CSYS Translation along Two Axes feature by selecting different locations in order to become more familiar with this feature Verification Session 8 14 CSYS Rotation along Axis • Check Enable Translation Increment and set a value • You can rotate along a single axis by hovering the mouse over a ring to highlight it, then click and drag around the origin to rotate. You will notice a black guide ring appear around the origin showing the direction of rotation. A number in black font to the top-right of the CSYS shows the angle in degrees of how much the object is being rotated. Once you release the left mouse button, the rotation will be applied. You will notice that the direction of the axes have changed. This is normal. This is to allow the user to translate in defined directions. It also represents how the object will appear if it is a regular CSYS being transformed. You can also apply rotations in the ‘Rotate’ number box. Just like the ‘Translate’ number box, the order of axes is X Y Z. For example, 0 0 30 would rotate the object by 30 degrees on the Z axis. This ignores incrementing. • Play with the CSYS Rotation along Axis feature by selecting different locations in order to become more familiar with this feature Ver…

课程类别：verification。课程编号 Session 9。
讲义原文摘录：
Verification Session 9 1 Session 9 Move and locate models In this session you will learn how to move and locate models by using some of Vericut’s modeling tools: Translate, Rotate, Assemble and Csys The Welcome Screen has opened file session_09_Move_and_locate_models.vcproject Verification Session 9 2 1. Move and locate the green block on the blue block using Assemble • In the Workpiece view, select the green block with numbers This highlights the STL model under the Green Block (0, 0, 0) We will re-orient the green block so the face #5 will be in the same plane as face D on the blue block. By using Mate, the selected faces will oppose each other. When using Align, the selected faces will both face in the same direction. • Configure > Assemble tab Note: The features on the Assemble tab enable you to move the selected object by assembling (mating or aligning) it with other objects • Select the arrow next to the first constraint Notice that the temporary messages area is indicating that you can now select on a feature , follow the prompts Verification Session 9 3 • Select face D on the Blue Block • Select face 5 on Green Block Verification Session 9 4 • Change Constraint Type to Align for the second constraint • Select the arrow next to the second constraint • Select face E on the Blue Block

topic: 故障与知识补齐: 缺少未知切削刀具参数_1794830088425 (Deep Excerpt)
content:
导读
刀具异常磨损、突发崩刃，是加工中心现场最常见的难题，不仅拉高刀具成本，还极易造成工件报废、生产中断。很多时候简单更换刀片治标不治本，只有认清各类失效形态，理解背后的切削机理，才能精准定位诱因、落地改善。
本文从破损形式、磨损机理到现场处置对策系统梳理，供工艺、调机与实训人员参考。
01 刀具破损的表现
1）切削刃微崩
当工件材料组织、硬度、余量不均匀，前角偏大造成切削刃强度不足，工艺系统刚性不足引发振动，或进行断续切削、刃磨质量较差时，切削刃易发生微崩，刃区出现微小崩落、缺口或剥落。发生微崩后刀具仍保有部分切削能力，可短时继续加工；但若持续切削，破损区域会快速扩展，演变为更严重的破损。
2）切削刃或刀尖崩碎
一般出现于比微崩更恶劣的切削条件，或是微崩进一步发展的结果。崩碎范围、尺寸更大，刀具直接丧失切削能力，必须停机更换；刀尖位置的崩碎，现场常称为掉尖。
3）刀片或刀具折断
切削载荷剧烈、切削用量过大、存在冲击载荷，刀片基体本身含有微裂纹，焊接、刃磨引入残余应力，叠加操作不当等因素，会造成刀片或刀体直接折断。属于一次性灾难性失效，刀具直接报废。
4）刀片表层剥落
高TiC硬质合金、陶瓷、PCBN等高脆性刀具材料，若表层存在组织缺陷、潜在微裂纹，或是焊接、刃磨引入表层残余应力，在切削交变接触应力作用下容易发生表层剥落。剥落可发生在前刀面，也可发生在后刀面，剥落形态多为片状，面积

检索刀具参数
检索刀具参数
可通过其参数来检索一个或一组切削刀具，并可在不同的制造过程中使用相同的参数。无需从头开始设置。使用
“刀具设定”(Tools Setup)
对话框中的
“文件”(File)
>
“打开参数文件”(Open Parameter File)
命令可检索单个或多个刀具。类似地，也可以使用
“刀具设定”(Tools Setup)
对话框中的
“文件”(File)
>
“打开刀具库”(Open Tool Library)
检索单个或多个刀具。
如果机床中存在与当前检索的切削刀具名称相同的切削刀具，而其类型和刀具参数与检索的刀具并不相同，则无法替换刀具。但是，如果刀具仅仅是偏移定义不同，则系统会提示确认替换。如果要检索较早的刀具，系统会使用当前参数来更新参数，并显示相应的消息。
检索版本 12.0 之前的刀具参数
在 Pro/ENGINEER 12.0 版之前的版本中，刀具参数文件的默认扩展名为
.tprm
，而对于 Pro/ENGINEER Wildfire 3.0 之前的版本，其扩展名为
.tpm
。Pro/ENGINEER Wildfire 4.0 可识别并检索具有这些扩展名的旧文件。
但是，用 Pro/ENGINEER Wildfire 4.0 修改或创建的刀具参数文件仅以
.xml
扩展名保存。
